title: Guidelines document block
description: Usage rules for an artifact. Each item pairs a rule with why it exists. Guidelines say what to do (or not do), and why.

guidelineEntry.description: One rule. `identifier` names the rule so other blocks and tools can point at it. `guidance` is the rule. `rationale` says why. `level` sets how strict it is. `category` groups it by discipline. `target` points at a specific part. `criteria` are tests that prove the rule holds. `references` cites outside standards like WCAG.

identifier.description: Optional name for this rule, unique within the entity (ex: 'one-primary-action', 'icon-only-needs-label'). MUST be lowercase kebab-case. Lets a test report, a linter, or an agent block cite the exact rule. Once published, an identifier MUST NOT be reused for a different rule. Retire it and make a new one instead.

guidance.description: The rule itself. MUST be concrete and clear (not 'use sparingly' or 'when possible').

rationale.description: Why the rule exists. Cite evidence, accessibility standards, or research when you have it. MUST NOT just repeat the guidance.

level.description: How strict the rule is: 'must' (breaking it is a defect), 'should' (follow it unless you have a good reason not to), 'should-not', or 'must-not'. Agents treat must/must-not as non-negotiable when writing or reviewing code.

evidence.description: Data backing this rule: test results, audit findings, or cited sources. Kept separate from `rationale` so tools can tell tested rules from convention. Use a plain string for a quick note, or the structured form so tools can read the finding and tell when it was gathered.

oneOf.description: A short prose note (ex: '9/10 agent test runs failed touch-target minimums below 36px').
Structured backing. `result` is the finding and `date` is when it was gathered. Both are required, so a rule can't rest on undated data. `method`, `sampleSize`, and `source` add detail.

result.description: What was found (ex: '9 of 10 runs failed the touch-target minimum').

date.description: When the evidence was gathered, as YYYY-MM-DD. Lets tools flag a rule resting on stale data.

method.description: How the evidence was gathered (ex: 'agent test harness', 'manual audit', 'usability study').

sampleSize.description: How many runs, participants, or cases the finding is based on.

source.description: Where to find the full evidence: a URL, issue reference, or report name.

category.description: Groups the rule by discipline: 'visual-design', 'interaction', 'accessibility', 'content', 'motion', or 'development'. Custom values allowed, in lowercase kebab-case.

target.description: The part this rule applies to (ex: 'label', 'icon'). Left out, it applies to the whole artifact.

refines.description: The `identifier` of a human guideline (in this entity's `documentBlocks`) that this rule sharpens. Used by agent-block rules to tighten a human rule (ex: an agent 'must-not' that hardens a human 'should'). When they conflict, the refining rule wins for agents. MUST be lowercase kebab-case and match a guideline identifier on the same entity.

criteria.description: Tests that prove this rule is met. Only add these when success can be objectively verified. Test results belong in `evidence`, not here.

references.description: Outside standards this rule follows (ex: WCAG, MDN, platform guidelines). Contains a URL and an optional label.

examples.description: Examples showing encouraged and discouraged approaches.

tags.description: Freeform keywords that relate guidelines across categories and disciplines (ex: 'rtl', 'localization', 'validation').

guidelines.description: Usage rules for an artifact (each a do/don't statement with a reason). Answers *how* to use it correctly. For *whether* to use it, see `use-cases`. For the opinion behind the rules (on foundations), see `principles`. Accessibility and content rules go here too (categories 'accessibility'/'content'). The `accessibility` and `content` blocks are for structured reference data, not rules.

items.description: The rules, in order. Tools SHOULD keep this order. Authors SHOULD lead with the most important or group by category.

kind.description: Identifies this block as a guidelines spec.
